extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and scientifically-interested public (readers of Popular Science Monthly); practitioners and students in applied sciences and public health
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and evaluating short popular-science magazine items (book notices, lecture reports, practical notes, and miscellany essays) aimed at a scientifically-curious lay and professional readership. Emphasizes clarity, usefulness, practical specifications, and selection of authorities/topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of water fit for domestic uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Such water should be wholesome, free from animalcules or other organisms, animal or vegetable, either living or dead, and at no time or season of the year, or in periods of epidemics, liable to propagate disease or cause the death of those who drink it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated qualities (Mr. Samuel C. Homersham): 1) wholesome and free from organisms liable to propagate disease; 2) soft and pleasant to use with soap for washing, bathing, and other detergent purposes, and of a quality that will not dissolve lead or form a deposit when boiled; 3) clear and bright, agreeable to the eye and refreshing to the taste; 4) well aerated, of nearly uniform normal temperature and not unduly warm in summer or unduly cold in winter (not like river/surface water). Recommendation: educate public opinion to insist upon these qualities; public works adequate to supply such water can often be constructed at moderate expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for promoting scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical measures to make the advancement of science more systematic and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six directives (Prof. R. H. Thurston): 1) determine most promising and important directions of exploration; 2) seek out and train young men fitted to be observers, discoverers, and philosophers and place them in positions where talents have scope; 3) obtain means of research and material aid—endowment of new schools, better organization, liberal provision of apparatus and material; 4) improve methods of instruction in science and enrich curricula (pure and applied), and make the teacher's position more desirable; 5) make academies and societies for advancement of science more thoroughly effective in organization and operation; 6) exhibit the community of interests between scientists and business men to encourage support and endowment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for artificial-cold quarantine treatment of yellow fever
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural and operational arrangements and temperature/handling rules for wards using artificial cold to treat yellow-fever patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements (Dr. Bushrod W. James): ward(s) at quarantine station arranged so ventilation is effected solely through ventilators and small anterooms with spring-doors; no other entrance/exit except through anteroom; anteroom should be kept at same or lower temperature than ward to avoid warming when doors open; maintain ward and anteroom at temperature not higher than 25° Fahr., making patients comfortable with sufficient bedclothing; everything leaving the room (clothing, excretions, emanations) must be exposed to the cold for sufficient time to destroy germs; if patients cannot bear cold, provide an adjoining warmer room accessible only through the cold room and require items leaving the warmer room to be retained long enough to rid contagion; if no attendant occupies anteroom, temperature may be kept near zero to more quickly destroy disease-producing agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for useful art hand-books for students
rubrics_metrics.description: Features that make small practical art hand-books valuable to art students and cultivators of practical art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable attributes (ascribed to Rowbotham and W. Williams hand-books): neat, concise little hand-books; prepared by experienced artists; tried and revised through many editions (proven usefulness); edited/issued by reputable editor (name as guarantee); reprinted/adapted for local use (American students); to be followed by other topical hand-books (series approach). Such features suggest usefulness to cultivators of practical art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for popular natural-history publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities that sustain interest and usefulness in a popular natural-history work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Native Flowers and Ferns of the United States' — sustained interest in recent numbers; colored illustrations should be beautifully life-like; accompanying text should be interesting and prepared with excellent judgment regarding what a popular work requires. Tone: cordial commendation when these features present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for valuable public science lectures/lecture series
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards by which public expository science lectures should be judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators of value (Science Lectures at South Kensington): subjects should be interesting; expositions should be popular but also thorough and trustworthy; authorities (lecturers) should be reputable/competent; lectures should cover useful apparatus and measurements for applied topics; a valuable series contains trustworthy expositions by recognized names in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for effective public-health guidance for parents and teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Desirable stylistic and practical attributes of short public-health manuals aimed at caretakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable traits (How to take Care of Our Eyes by H. C. Angell): very clear style; sparing use of technical terms; condensed and inexpensive (low price); full of useful, actionable suggestions which, if followed, prevent much annoyance and suffering from misuse of the eyes. Targeting parents and teachers implies accessible language and practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for engaging biographical sketches of lawyers
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes sketches of eminent lawyers readable and interesting rather than dull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable approach (Short Studies of Great Lawyers): not intended as full biographies but as estimates of character and career; should contain personal incident and delineation to enliven the sketches; aim to provide readable impressions rather than exhaustive life-histories; engaging style is valued because lawyers make interesting subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and performance specifications for grass-burner stove
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructional and operational features that make a grass/straw-burning stove suitable for settler households in regions lacking coal or timber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes from Prof. J. D. Butler (copied from Gardeners Monthly): material is unimportant (brick, stone, or sand/clay mix acceptable); stove size commonly large (examples: ~5 ft long, 6 ft high, 2.5 ft wide); erect centrally to heat multiple rooms; internal layout often has six 'stories'—ash-box; fire-box; cooking-oven; smoke-passage; hot-air chamber; smoke-passage to chimney or drum; fuel box about four feet long and ~1.5 ft wide/high; feed straw/grass with a fork; typical firing: pitch in grass/straw about 20 minutes two or at most three times in 24 hours for cooking/heating in Nebraska climate; scope for American improvements: make simpler, smaller, cheaper, better materials, more elegant design, and more economical combustion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a financially and socially viable silk-school farm project
rubrics_metrics.description: Project features and safeguards that would encourage capitalists and secure long-term success of a silk-school, farm, and village.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable provisions (Samuel Chamberlain's plan): provide legal interest on investment independent of silk production; return capital via improvement of real estate; secure profit beyond legal interest by retaining intermediate land sections expected to appreciate; provide growers of trees, silkworm eggs, and silk in addition to school production; rent forty cottages each with an acre of mulberry trees to foster cottage culture; train renters to become cottage-culture teachers who will demonstrate silk raising compatible with family duties; reduce strike risk by offering eventual ownership to renters; design the school to train habits of care and patience necessary for reeling silk; ensure long-term continuity (16–20 years) to build permanent local expertise and diffusion of the culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a drought-proof fodder plant
rubrics_metrics.description: Desired biological and agricultural properties making a plant suitable as fodder in drought-prone regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes observed for Caucasian prickly comfrey (Symphytum asperrimum): thrives in diverse climates and bears hot/dry seasons due to deep root penetration; two varieties (hollow vs. solid stem), with solid-stem variety excellent for stock and improving milk quantity/quality; rapid and luxuriant growth; high yield (example: 60–150 tons per acre vs. 8 tons for grass); reaches 4–5 ft near flowering with 3-ft leaves; flowers abundant in honey; easily propagated by stem cuttings with few eyes; perennial productivity for 15–20 years; fodder can be cut 6–8 times per year; leaves can be stacked green or partially dried with salt between layers to keep through winter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a valuable calculating machine for applied mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational and problem-domain features that indicate the utility of a calculating machine for high-level physical mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable qualities (ascribed to Prof. James Thomson's machine): simplicity of construction; mechanical robustness comparable favorably with notable inventions; ability to effect a variety of complicated calculations occurring in high-level applications of mathematics to physical problems; operable by unskilled labor to perform the work of many skilled arithmeticians in a given time; applicability to periodic phenomena (tides, magnetic and meteorological variations); capacity to solve second-order differential equations and perhaps higher orders; potential to reduce complex n-body gravitational problems (free motions of mutually-attracting particles) to the simple process of turning a crank.
